why: Resolving f first, a's ${?f} closes the cycle and is missing, so a is {t: 1} and f is a.t then x, "1x". Resolving a first, f's ${?a.t} closes it, f is "x", and a is the object {t: 1} followed by the text "x", an error (L373-374, L384-385). f = "x" together with a = {t: 1} needs both optionals missing at once, which no order gives: a cycle is broken by removing one of its links (L660-661), the optional that closes it (L714-716), and the order is undefined, so either result or an error is allowed (L866-881). typesafe/config gives f = "x", a = {t: 1}; in 044, the same cycle without the x, it gives f = 1
